question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic secant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsech}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{x\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[2\operatorname{arsech}⁡(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)] \\  & =2\cdot [-\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x\sqrt{1-{cos}^{2}⁡x}}]\cdot {(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}^{′} \\  & =-\frac{2}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡x}}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\  & =2\operatorname{sec}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
